title: Vitruvian tool protocol: one message
description: One line on the link between the app and a tool: a JSON-RPC 2.0 message, in UTF-8, with no line break inside it, at most 1,048,576 bytes long. methods.json lists every message; each message's params and result are a definition below. A field this schema does not name is ignored, which is how a later version adds one. Version 2 adds the six ui/ messages and what they carry, and changes nothing of version 1.

id.description: What ties an answer to its request. A whole number or a string, chosen by whoever sends the request. The app counts up from 1.

request.description: A message that is answered. The answer is a result or a failure with the same id.

method.description: Which message this is. One the receiver does not know is answered with failure -32601.

params.description: What the message carries. Always an object.

notice.description: A message that is not answered. It has no id.

method.description: Which message this is. One the receiver does not know is ignored.

params.description: What the message carries. Always an object.

result.description: The answer to a request that was done.
What the request's row in methods.json names. Always an object.

failure.description: The answer to a request that was not done.

id.description: The request's id, or null when the request could not be read at all.

error.description: Why a request was not done. Codes: -32700 the line was not JSON; -32600 it was not a message; -32601 the method is not known; -32602 its params are wrong; -32603 something broke inside. A refusal by the app: -32001 the service is not listed in the tool's uses; -32002 the tool is not installed; -32003 Vitruvian lacks a macOS permission the service needs; -32004 not available right now. A refusal by the tool: -32010 the command was not run. A tool must cope with any request being refused.

message.description: The reason, in a few English words, for a log. Never shown to the person as it is.

data.description: More about the reason. For -32001 and -32003 it is a refusalData.

service.description: For -32001: the entry missing from the tool's uses.

permission.description: For -32003: the macOS permission Vitruvian lacks, for example accessibility.

empty.description: Nothing to say: an object with no fields. It is the result of a request that was simply done.

initializeParams.description: The first message. Until it is answered neither side sends anything else.

protocolVersions.description: The protocol versions the app speaks.

language.description: The language the app is in, as a tag such as en-US, fr or pt-BR.

dataFolder.description: The folder the tool may keep its own files in. It is also the folder the tool is started in.

features.description: What this app has beyond the first release of the protocol version, by name: ui.status, ui.choice, preferences.options, ui.status.activity. A name the tool does not know is ignored. An app before 3.48 sends none, and has none of them; 3.48 and 3.49 send the first three.

initializeResult.description: The tool's answer to initialize. A tool that picks a version the app did not offer is stopped.

protocolVersion.description: The one version, of those offered, the tool will speak.

commandRunParams.description: Run one of the tool's commands. The answer is empty when it ran, or failure -32010 when the tool would not run it.

command.description: The command's id as the manifest writes it, without the tool's id in front.

preferencesChangedParams.description: Some of the tool's preferences were changed from outside the tool.

values.description: Each changed preference's id and its new value.

languageChangedParams.description: The person changed the app's language.

language.description: The new language, as a tag.

commandsStateParams.description: Which of the tool's commands can run now. The tool sends it whenever that changes; each one replaces the last. Until the first one, all of them can.

runnable.description: The ids of the commands that can run. A command not listed cannot.

notifyHUDParams.description: Show the app's short on-screen message.

icon.description: An SF Symbol name, drawn beside the message.

message.description: The words, shown as the tool wrote them.

openURLParams.description: Open a link in the person's default app for it.

opened.description: False when macOS had nothing to open it with.

text.description: The clipboard's text. Left out when the clipboard holds no text.

clipboardWriteTextParams.description: Replace the clipboard with this text, marked as Vitruvian's own so clipboard history files it correctly.

clipboardWriteTextResult.description: Whether the clipboard took the text.

written.description: False when the clipboard would not take it.

keystrokesPasteParams.description: Paste this text into the app in front. The clipboard is put back afterwards.

keystrokesPressMenuItemParams.description: Press a menu item of the app in front, found by its key equivalent and never by its title.

equivalents.description: The key equivalents that count. The first enabled item that has one of them is pressed.

keyEquivalent.description: A menu item's key equivalent. Command is always part of it.

character.description: The key, as the menu shows it, for example V.

pressed.description: False when no enabled item has one of the key equivalents.

processesTerminateParams.description: End a process, with the app's checks and its administrator prompt when one is needed.

name.description: The process's name, shown if the app has to ask for an administrator password.

force.description: True to end it at once; false to ask it to quit.

storageGetParams.description: Read one of the preferences the manifest declares.

value.description: The saved value, or the manifest's default when nothing is saved.

storageSetParams.description: Save one of the preferences the manifest declares.

value.description: The new value, of the type the manifest names. Text is at most 4,096 characters: the app answers a longer one with failure -32602 and saves nothing.

logParams.description: A line for the tool's log in Settings.

uiOpenParams.description: The person opened one of the tool's panels. A blocks panel is answered with its first page; a web panel with {}.

panel.description: The panel's id, as the manifest gives it.

tree.description: The first page. Left out for a web panel, and for a page the tool will send later with ui/render.

uiEventParams.description: The person acted in an open panel. Answered with the next page, or with keep.

block.description: The id of the block the person acted on. Left out for bridge.

event.description: What the person did. tap: a button, a row or a list's row was pressed. toggle: a switch was turned. submit: Return was pressed in a field. change: a field was left with other text in it, or an option of a choice was picked. bridge: a web panel's page called window.vitruvian.call.

value.description: For toggle, the switch's new state. For submit and change, the field's text; for the change of a choice, the picked option's value. For a tap on a list's row, the row's id. For bridge, an object: method, the request the page made, and params, what it carries. A tool sends such a request to the app as its own; a method that starts with tool/ is the tool's own.

uiEventResult.description: The answer to ui/event. With no tree, or with keep, the page stays as it is.

keep.description: True: the page stays as it is.

reply.description: For bridge: what the page's call gets back.

open.description: A window panel of the same tool to open, in answer to what the person did. A tool cannot open a window at any other time.

uiCloseParams.description: The panel went away: the person closed it, or the app did.

uiRenderParams.description: A new page for a panel that is open, sent unprompted. The app draws at most four a second for each panel, the last one of the ones between; more than forty in one second is a flood, and the tool is stopped. One for a panel the manifest does not declare, or that is not open, is dropped.

uiBadgeParams.description: A count or a dot beside the tool's page in the island's Explore gallery. With neither, the badge goes. Needs notify in the manifest's uses.

count.description: A whole number from 0. 0 is no count.

dot.description: True for a dot, when there is no count.

uiStatusParams.description: The tool's status: a small mark the app draws on the closed island. Each one replaces the last, and it goes when the tool's program ends. The manifest must declare it, under contributes.status: without that the app answers failure -32602. The person can switch it off for the tool; it is then still answered with {} and nothing is drawn. activity and since are drawn only when the manifest's status says activity: true; otherwise they are left out and the mark is drawn. An app before 3.48 answers failure -32601.

state.description: none: no mark. ok: all is well. busy: something is under way. attention: something waits for the person. failure: something failed.

text.description: What it means, in one short line, for VoiceOver and the tooltip. Shown as one line of at most 120 characters. Left out, the app says its own word for the state.

icon.description: An SF Symbol name, drawn in place of the state's own glyph. The colour, the size and the motion stay the app's. A name this Mac does not have, or a blank one, draws the state's own glyph.

activity.description: A few words for the closed island, drawn beside the mark while it is the one shown, in place of the allowance percent. Cut to one line of 12 characters and drawn in about 30 points: six characters or fewer, and a number is best. Blank counts as absent. Ignored for none. An app before 3.50 ignores it.

since.description: Unix time in seconds, a fraction allowed. The app shows the seconds since then when there is no activity, and counts them itself. A time in the future shows 0. An app before 3.50 ignores it.

uiTree.description: A page: blocks, drawn one under the other. At most 262,144 bytes as JSON, an image written into it included: the app does not draw a larger one, and the tool's log says so.

uiBlock.description: One block. type says which of the thirteen kinds it is, and the kind's own fields go beside it. A kind the app does not know is drawn as its fallback, or left out: that is how a later version adds one.

type.description: The kind: text, heading, row, button, toggle, field, list, progress, image, divider, link, spacer or choice.

id.description: The block's name within the page, as the events it causes name it. Required for button, toggle, field, list and choice; a row with one can be tapped. The same characters as a command id.

fallback.description: What an app that does not know this kind draws instead, as plain text.

localizedText.description: Text in one or more languages, keyed by language tag, as a manifest's text is. English, under en, is required.

uiText.description: Text the person reads: a string, or one entry per language. Drawn as written, never as markdown.

style.description: body when left out. secondary and caption are quieter; monospaced is for code and logs.

lines.description: The most lines the words take. 4 when left out.

headingBlock.description: A heading, of two lines at most.

rowBlock.description: One line that stands alone. With an id it can be tapped.

trailing.description: A few words at the row's end, such as a time.

buttonBlock.description: A button. Pressing it is the event tap.

style.description: plain when left out. prominent is the page's main action; destructive one that deletes.

enabled.description: False draws it dimmed, and it cannot be pressed.

toggleBlock.description: A switch. Turning it is the event toggle, with its new state.

enabled.description: False draws it dimmed, and it cannot be turned.

fieldBlock.description: A field to type in. Return is the event submit; leaving it with other text is the event change.

title.description: What it is for, above it.

placeholder.description: What it shows while it is empty.

kind.description: text when left out. number takes digits; secret hides what is typed.

id.description: The row's name, as a tap on it names it.

trailing.description: A few words at the row's end.

listBlock.description: Rows, drawn together. Tapping one is the event tap; its value is the row's id.

value.description: From 0 to 1. Left out, it is under way and nobody knows how far.

source.description: A file in the tool's folder, as a path inside it, or the picture itself as a data: address of a PNG or JPEG. It counts toward the page's 262,144 bytes.

height.description: Its height in points, up to 300. The app's own when left out.

dividerBlock.description: A line between blocks. It has no fields.

linkBlock.description: A link the app opens through its open service, so the manifest must list open in uses: without it, a click plays the alert sound.

size.description: In points, up to 40. 8 when left out.

value.description: What the event carries when the person picks it. At most 128 characters. It may be empty.

title.description: What the menu shows for it, as one line.

choiceBlock.description: A pop-up menu: one of a fixed list of options. Picking one is the event change, with the option's value. No two options share a value: JSON Schema cannot say that, and the app refuses a page that breaks it. An app before 3.48 does not know this kind and draws its fallback, which nobody can change: ask the app for ui.choice first, and send a field to an app without it.

title.description: What is being chosen, beside the menu.

value.description: The selected option's value. One that is no option's is drawn as an extra first row, as written.

enabled.description: False draws it dimmed, and nothing can be picked.
